# PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME] Scope and interpretation

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME] 1. This Practice Direction is made under rule 51.2. It provides for a pilot scheme under which claims to which the pilot applies are to be referred automatically for mediation provided by the Mediation Service (which has the meaning given in rule 26.6(3)).

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME] 2. The pilot is to run from 22 May 2024 to 6 April 2027 and applies to claims issued on or after 22 May 2024.

## 3.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] The pilot applies –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] (a) to claims to which rule 26.6, as modified by this practice direction, applies; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] (b) to “OCMC mediation pilot claims”, being claims within scope of Practice Direction 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] (i) that are suitable for allocation to the small claims track; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] (ii) that are not road traffic accident claims.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 3.] Modification of rules during the pilot

## 4. During the pilot, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will apply –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 4. During the pilot, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will apply –] (a) with the modifications set out in paragraphs 6 to 10 of this practice direction; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 4. During the pilot, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will apply –] (b) in relation to OCMC mediation pilot claims, with the provisions contained in PD 51R – Online Civil Money Claims Pilot which operate at the stage  where following a defence, a claimant has confirmed they intend to  proceed, the claim is stayed and referred to the small claims mediation  service.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 4. During the pilot, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will apply –] Rules 26.6, 27.8, 27.14 and 45.13 and the relevant provision of Practice Direction 27A as so modified are set out in the annex to this practice direction.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 4. During the pilot, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will apply –] 5. For claims to which the pilot does not apply, the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions will continue to apply without modification.

## 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] (a) for paragraph (2) substitute—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] “(2) This rule—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] (a) applies where the only remedy claimed is, or purports to be, a judgment for a specified sum of money; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] (c) does not in any event apply to road traffic accident or personal injury claims.”;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] (b) in paragraph (4), for the words “indicate” to “mediation” substitute “have filed their directions questionnaire”;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] (c) after paragraph (5) insert—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 6. Modification of rule 26.6: Rule 26.6 is modified as follows—] “(6) If a claim to which this rule applies proceeds to a final hearing, the court must consider at that hearing whether any sanction is appropriate in all the circumstances having regard to whether the parties attended mediation provided by the Mediation Service.”.

## 7. Modification of rule 27.8:  In rule 27.8, after paragraph (6) insert—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 7. Modification of rule 27.8:  In rule 27.8, after paragraph (6) insert—] “(7) The court must consider whether any sanction is appropriate in all the circumstances having regard to whether the parties attended mediation provided by the Mediation Service.”.

## 8 .       Modification of rule 27.14:  In rule 27.14, after paragraph (2) insert—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 8 .       Modification of rule 27.14:  In rule 27.14, after paragraph (2) insert—] “(2A) When considering how to exercise its discretion to order or decline to order costs falling within paragraph (2) (including when considering under paragraph (2)(g) whether a party has behaved unreasonably), the court may also take into account any failure by a party to attend mediation provided by the Mediation Service under rule 26.6.”.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 8 .       Modification of rule 27.14:  In rule 27.14, after paragraph (2) insert—] 9. Modification of Practice Direction 27A:  In Appendix B, for the first standard direction substitute—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 8 .       Modification of rule 27.14:  In rule 27.14, after paragraph (2) insert—] “ 1. Each party must deliver to every other party and to the court office copies of all documents on which they intend to rely at the hearing no later than [                        ] [14 days before the hearing]. (These should include the letter making the claim and the reply; and, if a party failed to attend mediation provided by the Mediation Service, that party’s explanation for that failure, and any other party’s comments on the matter, with any supporting documents.)”.

## 10. Modification of rule 45.13:  After paragraph (2) insert—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 10. Modification of rule 45.13:  After paragraph (2) insert—] “(2A) The court may also make an order under paragraph (1) or (2) on its own initiative in any case where rule 26.6(6) applies.”.

## 11. Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 11. Omitted] __________________________________________________________________

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51ZE – SMALL CLAIMS TRACK AUTOMATIC REFERRAL TO MEDIATION PILOT SCHEME > 11. Omitted] ANNEX: RULES AS MODIFIED

# PART 26

[PART 26] Referral to the Mediation Service

[PART 26] 26.6.— (1) This rule applies to claims started in the County Court which would normally be allocated to the small claims track pursuant to rule 26.9.

[PART 26] (2) This rule—

[PART 26] (a) applies where the only remedy claimed is, or purports to be, a specified sum of money;

[PART 26] (b) does not apply to a claim which is started using Online Civil Money Claims; and

[PART 26] (c) does not in any event apply to road traffic accident or personal injury claims.

[PART 26] (3) In this rule, ‘the Mediation Service’ means the Small Claims Mediation Service operated by His Majesty’s Courts and Tribunals Service.

[PART 26] (4) Where all parties have filed their directions questionnaire, the claim will be referred to the Mediation Service.

[PART 26] (5) If a claim to which this rule applies is settled, the proceedings will automatically be stayed with permission to apply for—

[PART 26] (a) judgment for the unpaid balance of the outstanding sum of the settlement agreement; or

[PART 26] (b) the claim to be restored for hearing of the full amount claimed,

[PART 26] unless the parties have agreed that the claim is to be discontinued or dismissed.

[PART 26] (6) If a claim to which this rule applies proceeds to a final hearing, the court must consider at that hearing whether any sanction is appropriate in all the circumstances having regard to whether the parties attended mediation provided by the Mediation Service.

# PART 27

[PART 27] Conduct of the hearing

## 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (2) Hearings will be informal.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (3) The strict rules of evidence do not apply.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (4) The court need not take evidence on oath.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (5) The court may limit cross-examination.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (6) The court must give reasons for its decision.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] (7) The court must consider whether any sanction is appropriate in all the circumstances having regard to whether the parties attended mediation provided by the Mediation Service.

[PART 27 > 27.8.— (1) The court may adopt any method of proceeding at a hearing that it considers to be fair.] Costs on the small claims track

## 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (Rules 46.11 and 46.13 make provision in relation to orders for costs made before a claim has been allocated to the small claims track)

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (2) The court may not order a party to pay a sum to another party in respect of that other party’s costs, fees and expenses, including those relating to an appeal, except–

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (a) the fixed costs attributable to issuing the claim which–

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (i) are payable under Part 45; or

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (ii) would be payable under Part 45 if that Part applied to the claim;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (b) in proceedings which included a claim for an injunction or an order for specific performance a sum not exceeding the amount specified in Practice Direction 27A for legal advice and assistance relating to that claim;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (c) any court fees paid by that other party;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (d) expenses which a party or witness has reasonably incurred in travelling to and from a hearing or in staying away from home for the purposes of attending a hearing;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (e) a sum not exceeding the amount specified in Practice Direction 27A for any loss of earnings or loss of leave by a party or witness due to attending a hearing or to staying away from home for the purposes of attending a hearing;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (f) a sum not exceeding the amount specified in Practice Direction 27A for an expert’s fees;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (g) such further costs as the court may assess by the summary procedure and order to be paid by a party who has behaved unreasonably;

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (h) the Stage 1 and, where relevant, the Stage 2 fixed costs in rule 45.18 where–

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (i) the claim was within the scope of the Pre-Action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury Claims in Road Traffic Accidents (‘the RTA Protocol’) or the Pre-action Protocol for Low Value Personal Injury (Employers’ Liability and Public Liability) Claims (‘the EL/PL Protocol’);

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (ii) the claimant reasonably believed that the claim was valued at more than the small claims track limit in accordance with paragraph 4.1(4) of the relevant Protocol; and

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (iii) the defendant admitted liability under the process set out in the relevant Protocol; but

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (iv) the defendant did not pay those Stage 1 and, where relevant, Stage 2 fixed costs; and

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (i) in an appeal, the cost of any approved transcript reasonably incurred.

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (2A) When considering how to exercise its discretion to order or decline to order costs falling within paragraph (2) (including when considering under paragraph (2)(g) whether a party has behaved unreasonably), the court may also take into account any failure by a party to attend mediation provided by the Mediation Service under rule 26.6.

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (3) A party’s rejection of an offer in settlement will not of itself constitute unreasonable behaviour under paragraph (2)(g) but the court may take it into consideration when it is applying the unreasonableness test.

[PART 27 > 27.14.— (1) This rule applies to any case which has been allocated to the small claims track.] (4) The limits on costs imposed by this rule also apply to any fee or reward for acting on behalf of a party to the proceedings charged by a person exercising a right of audience by virtue of an order under section 11 of the Courts and Legal Services Act 1990 (a lay representative).

# PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A] Appendix B: STANDARD DIRECTIONS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A] (For use where the district judge specifies no other directions)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A] THE COURT DIRECTS:

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A] 1. Each party must deliver to every other party and to the court office copies of all documents on which they intend to rely at the hearing no later than [                        ] [14 days before the hearing]. (These should include the letter making the claim and the reply; and, if a party failed to attend mediation provided by the Mediation Service, that party’s explanation for that failure, and any other party’s comments on the matter, with any supporting documents.)

## 2 The original documents must be brought to the hearing.

## 3 [Notice of hearing date and time allowed.]

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A > 3 [Notice of hearing date and time allowed.]] 4 The parties are encouraged to contact each other with a view to trying to settle the case or narrow the issues. However the court must be informed immediately if the case is settled by agreement before the hearing date.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A > 3 [Notice of hearing date and time allowed.]] 5 No party may rely at the hearing on any report from an expert unless express permission has been granted by the court beforehand. Anyone wishing to rely on an expert must write to the court immediately on receipt of this Order and seek permission, giving an explanation why the assistance of an expert is necessary.

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 27A > 3 [Notice of hearing date and time allowed.]] NOTE: Failure to comply with the directions may result in the case being adjourned and in the party at fault having to pay costs. The parties are encouraged always to try to settle the case by negotiating with each other. The court must be informed immediately if the case is settled before the hearing.”

# PART 45

[PART 45] Unreasonable behaviour

[PART 45] 45.13. —(1) Where, in a claim to which Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of this Part applies, an order for costs is made in favour of a party whom the court considers has behaved unreasonably, the other party may apply for an order that those costs be reduced by an amount equivalent to 50% of the fixed recoverable costs which would otherwise be payable.

[PART 45] (2) Where, in a claim to which Section VI, Section VII or Section VIII of this Part applies, an order for costs is made against a party whom the court considers has behaved unreasonably, the other party may apply for an order that those costs be increased by an amount equivalent to 50% of the fixed recoverable costs which would otherwise be payable.

[PART 45] (2A) The court may also make an order under paragraph (1) or (2) on its own initiative in any case where rule 26.6(6) applies.

[PART 45] (3) In this rule—

[PART 45] (a) unreasonable behaviour is conduct for which there is no reasonable explanation; and

[PART 45] (b) “fixed recoverable costs which would otherwise be payable” does not include—

[PART 45] (i) VAT;

[PART 45] (ii)any additional amounts under rules 36.17 or 36.24; or (iii)any disbursements.
